Yet this is not had from the text, unless perhaps from Eve's answer cited above; which, however, can be understood thus: that these commands were given first and immediately to the man, and to the woman through him.

paras.t: Quinto quæritur, anne etiam alia præcepta data sunt eis. Et videtur quod sic, quoniam tenebantur ad legem naturalem et ejus præcepta. Tenebantur quoque vitare peccata mortalia divinis præceptis directe contraria : imo obligabantur credere et sperare in Deum, et diligere eum præ omnibus. Denique in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Deus ab initio constituit hominem, adjecit illi præcepta et mandata. Amplius, ista præcepta non erant nisi de corporalibus rebus, sed Deus exigit a primis parentibus spiritualem subjectionem et cultum internum, ergo dedit eis præcepta de talibus. Ad istud respondendum est affirmative, sicut argumenta hæc probant, quod etiam clarius comprobatur ex his, quæ in Ecclesiastico scribuntur : Deus de terra creavit hominem, creavit ex ipso adjutorium simile sibi. Disciplina intellectus replevit eos, creavit illis scientiam spiritus, sensu implevit corda illorum, bona et mala ostendit illis, justitiam et judicia sua ostendit illis, et dixit illis : Attendite ab omni iniquo.
paras.en: Fifthly, it is asked whether other precepts too were given them. And it seems so, since they were bound to the natural law and its precepts. They were bound also to avoid mortal sins directly contrary to the divine precepts; nay, they were obliged to believe and hope in God, and to love him above all things. Lastly, it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 15:14|God made man from the beginning|Deus ab initio constituit hominem]], [[Ecclus 15:15|He added his commandments and precepts|adjecit illi præcepta et mandata]] [the margin note here could not be read; Denis gives Ecclus 15:14–15 freely, 'he added to him precepts and commandments']. Further, these precepts concerned only bodily things, but God requires of our first parents a spiritual subjection and inward worship; therefore he gave them precepts about such things. To this one must answer in the affirmative, as these arguments prove; and it is proved still more clearly from what is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 17:1|God created man of the earth|Deus de terra creavit hominem]], [[Ecclus 17:5|He created of him a helpmate like to himself|creavit ex ipso adjutorium simile sibi]]; [[Ecclus 17:5|he filled them with the knowledge of understanding|Disciplina intellectus replevit eos]]. [[Ecclus 17:6|He created in them the science of the spirit, he fired their heart with wisdom, and shewed them both good and evil|creavit illis scientiam spiritus, sensu implevit corda illorum, bona et mala ostendit illis]], [[Ecclus 17:10|he shewed them his justice and judgments|justitiam et judicia sua ostendit illis]], and [[Ecclus 17:11|he said to them: Beware of all iniquity|dixit illis : Attendite ab omni iniquo]] [this margin note could not be read either; the words are gathered from Ecclus 17:1, 5–6, 10–11].

paras.t: Sexto quæritur, qualiter et in qua lingua locutus est illis Deus, et qualiter potuerunt intelligere aliquod idioma. Ad hoc Augustinus obscure respondet, et sentire videtur, quod per creaturam subjectam, puta per angelum, locutus sit et jusserit illis duo illa præcepta. Scholastica quoque historia et Henricus de Hassia, clarius id affirmant. Et addit Henricus, quod in Hebræo facta sit illa locutio. Atque secundum Augustinum, dicendum quod sicut Deus concreavit illis scientiam, ita et Hebrææ loquelæ peritiam.
paras.en: Sixthly, it is asked how, and in what language, God spoke to them, and how they could understand any tongue. To this Augustine answers obscurely, and seems to hold that he spoke and enjoined those two precepts upon them through a creature subject to him, for instance through an angel. The Scholastic History too, and Henry of Hesse, affirm this more clearly. And Henry adds that this speech was made in Hebrew. And, following Augustine, it must be said that as God concreated knowledge with them [that is, created it in them together with their nature], so too he gave them skill in the Hebrew speech.

paras.t: Septimo quæritur, qualiter et quibus dixit Deus. Non est bonum hominem esse solum, faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi. Respondetur quod Deus hoc dixit, id est, intra se cogitavit ac definivit, ita quod dicere sumitur hic essentialiter pro practica intellectione. Et ista locutio est totius superbeatissimæ Trinitatis ad se, vel Patris ad Filium ac Spiritum Sanctum, quemadmodum dictum est super illud : Dixit Deus, Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram.
paras.en: Seventhly, it is asked how, and to whom, God said: [[2:18|It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself|Non est bonum hominem esse solum, faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi]]. The answer is that God said this, that is, thought and determined it within himself; so that *to say* is taken here essentially [that is, as said of the divine essence common to the three Persons, not of one Person], for a practical act of understanding. And this utterance is that of the whole most supremely blessed Trinity to itself, or of the Father to the Son and the Holy Ghost, as was said on the words: God said, [[Gen 1:26|Let us make man to our image and likeness|Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram]].

paras.t: Octavo quæritur, cur Dominus volens tollere unam de costis Adæ, etc., misit soporem in eum. Ad hoc quidam respondet, ne Adam videret costæ suæ amotionem. Sed contra hoc objici posset, quia secundum Augustinum, sopor ille non est missus in Adam, ne sentiret dolorem ex costæ abstractione, quia et vigilanti potuit eam sine dolore avellere : ergo a fortiori apparet, quod non sit facta soporis immissio, ne Adam videret costæ suæ sublationem, quia et invisibiliter potuit eam Deus auferre. Denique sublatio costæ, non est corporaliter et visibiliter facta, per applicationem manus aut alterius membri aut instrumenti, sed jussu Omnipotentis, aut etiam invisibili aliquo cooperatu angelico. Sunt igitur hujus rei aliæ rationes. Prima, quoniam Deus dum costam abstulit, voluit viro revelare mysterium seu causam ablationis illius : ideo misit in eum contemplationis soporem et ecstasim, in qua revelavit ei multa secreta et spiritualem rationem facti illius : quæ tamen ratio in se spiritualis, fuit litteralis ibidem, sicut et sequens, secundum Augustinum. Secunda itaque ratio est, quia per formationem Evæ ex Adam, voluit Deus præfigurare formationem Ecclesiæ ex Christo : idcirco ex Adam dormiente et soporato Deus formavit Evam, quia prævidit quod ex Christo dormiente in cruce, formanda esset Ecclesia.
paras.en: Eighthly, it is asked why the Lord, when he wished to take [[2:21|one of his ribs|unam de costis Adæ]] from Adam, etc., [[2:21|cast a deep sleep upon|misit soporem]] him. To this a certain writer answers: lest Adam should see the removal of his rib. But against this it could be objected that, according to Augustine, that sleep was not sent into Adam lest he should feel pain from the drawing out of the rib, since God could have plucked it out without pain even while he was awake: therefore a fortiori it appears that the sleep was not sent lest Adam should see the taking away of his rib, since God could also have removed it invisibly. Moreover, the taking of the rib was not done bodily and visibly, by the application of a hand or of another member or of an instrument, but by the command of the Almighty, or else by some invisible cooperation of angels. There are therefore other reasons for this. The first: because God, while he took the rib, willed to reveal to the man the mystery or cause of that taking away; therefore he sent into him the sleep of contemplation, and ecstasy, in which he revealed to him many secrets and the spiritual reason of that deed: which reason, though spiritual in itself, was there the literal sense, as was the following one too, according to Augustine. The second reason, then, is that by the forming of Eve from Adam God willed to prefigure the forming of the Church from Christ: therefore God formed Eve from Adam sleeping and cast into a deep sleep, because he foresaw that the Church was to be formed from Christ sleeping on the cross.

paras.t: Nono quæritur, cur Deus formavit mulierem ex viro, et non potius ambos simul produxit de communi materia, sicut in ceteris animalibus fecit. Et respondendum quod ideo. Primo, ut vir conjugem magis diligeret, non solum tanquam aliquid simile sibi, sed et tanquam aliquid sui, et tanquam quemdam sui effectum. Hinc duodecimo de Civitate Dei loquitur Augustinus : Quod ex latere viri facta est mulier, signat quam cara debet esse conjunctio mariti et conjugis. Secundo, ut in hoc quoque primus homo Deo assimilaretur, quod sicut omnia sunt ex Deo, sic universum genus humanum prodiret ex uno homine primo. Tertio, quoniam vir caput est mulieris : ideireo ex eo tanquam a quodam principio fuerat procreanda. Quarto, ut femina suo marito fidelius et amorosius adhæreret tanquam principio suo. Quinto, propter significationem mysterii, utpote quod tota Ecclesia esset formanda a Christo.
paras.en: Ninthly, it is asked why God formed the woman from the man, and did not rather bring forth both at once from a common matter, as he did in the other animals. And the answer must be that he did so for these reasons. First, that the man might love his wife the more, not only as something like himself, but also as something of his own, and as a certain effect of himself. Hence Augustine says in the twelfth book of the City of God: That the woman was made from the side of the man signifies how dear the union of husband and wife ought to be. Secondly, that in this too the first man might be made like to God: that as all things are from God, so the whole human race should come forth from one first man. Thirdly, because the man is the head of the woman: therefore she was to be produced from him as from a kind of principle. Fourthly, that the woman might cleave more faithfully and lovingly to her husband as to her principle. Fifthly, for the signification of the mystery, namely that the whole Church was to be formed from Christ.

paras.t: Decimo quæritur, quare potius de costa et latere Adæ sumpta est Eva. Respondetur, ad designandum quod Ecclesia esset formanda de sanguine ex Christi latere profluente. Item ad innuendum, quod uxor sit juxta sui mariti latus ponenda et tanquam socia, non quasi ancilla aut domina a viro suo habenda : ideireo de media corporis parte, videlicet costa, non de capite aut pede viri est facta.
paras.en: Tenthly, it is asked why Eve was taken rather from the rib and side of Adam. The answer is: to signify that the Church was to be formed from the blood flowing from Christ's side[[John 19:34||]]. Also to intimate that a wife is to be placed beside her husband's side, and to be held by her husband as a companion, not as a handmaid or a mistress: therefore she was made from the middle part of the body, namely a rib, not from the head or the foot of the man.

paras.t: Undecimo quæritur de contemplatione Adæ in præfato sopore, qualiter viderit Deum, et quid ex divina revelatione tunc cognoverit. Respondetur quod non vidit Deum clare per speciem, sed contemplatione anagogica ac mystica multum præclara, quæ fuit quasi medio modo se habens inter beatificam patriæ visionem, et communem contemplationem Dei in via. Denique, secundum doctores, ex divina revelatione tunc cognovit Dei Filium incarnandum, non tamen cognovit tunc causam Incarnationis, videlicet quod pro diluendis mundi peccatis esset incarnandus : non enim præscivit ruinam suam. Et quod istud sit verum, ex eo perpenditur, quod Adam evigilans et reversus ad se, prophetavit : Relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem suam, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una. Quod exponens Apostolus : Sacramentum, inquit, hoc magnum est ; ego autem dico in Christo et in Ecclesia. Intellexit itaque Adam in raptu illo, feminam de costa sua esse formatam, et rationem formationis illius ac designationem matrimonii tunc instituti, ut est in naturæ officium.
paras.en: Eleventhly, it is asked about Adam's contemplation in the said sleep: how he saw God, and what he then knew by divine revelation. The answer is that he did not see God clearly by sight [that is, in his essence, as the blessed see him], but by an anagogical and mystical contemplation of great brightness, which stood as it were midway between the beatific vision of the fatherland and the common contemplation of God in the way [that is, between the vision of the blessed in heaven and the contemplation of wayfarers in this life]. Further, according to the doctors, he then knew by divine revelation that the Son of God was to be incarnate; yet he did not then know the cause of the Incarnation, namely that he was to be incarnate to wash away the sins of the world: for he did not foreknow his own fall. And that this is true is gathered from the fact that Adam, awaking and come back to himself, prophesied: [[2:24|a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh|Relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem suam, et adhærebit uxori suæ, et erunt duo in carne una]]. Expounding which, the Apostle says: [[Eph 5:32|This is a great sacrament: but I speak in Christ and in the church|Sacramentum, inquit, hoc magnum est ; ego autem dico in Christo et in Ecclesia]]. So Adam understood in that rapture that the woman had been formed from his rib, and the reason of her formation, and the meaning of the marriage then instituted, as it is for the office of nature [that is, marriage as ordained for the begetting of offspring, as distinct from marriage as a remedy after the Fall].

paras.t: In Scholastica quoque historia fertur : Evigilans prophetavit de conjunctione Christi et Ecclesiæ, et ibidem cognovit de futuro diluvio, judicium quoque futurum per ignem, ac suis liberis indicavit. Verumtamen istud reor incertum, quod cognovit de futuro diluvio atque judicio Dei per ignem. Sic enim, ut apparet, præcognovisset sui ac posteritatis suæ ruinam, eo quod diluvium et ignis judicium, directe instituunt pœnam. In cujus ratione datur intelligi culpa præcedens, quod illuminatissimum Adam non latuit. Et quamvis post primam Protoplasti transgressionem, interdum infligitur pœna absque prævia (pro qua infligatur) culpa, tamen si primus homo non peccasset, non infligeretur posteris pœna sine prævia culpa : quod etiam S. Thomas affirmat. Porro incarnatio Filii Dei non supplicium, sed potius beneficium denotat.
paras.en: In the Scholastic History, too, it is reported: Awaking, he prophesied of the union of Christ and the Church; and there too he knew of the flood to come, and also of the judgment to come by fire, and made them known to his children. Yet I think it uncertain that he knew of the flood to come and of God's judgment by fire. For in that case, as it appears, he would have foreknown his own fall and that of his posterity, since the flood and the judgment of fire are directly a punishment; and in the very notion of punishment a preceding fault is given to be understood, which would not have been hidden from Adam, enlightened as he was in the highest degree. And although, after the first transgression of the Protoplast [that is, the first-formed man, Adam], punishment is sometimes inflicted without a previous fault (for which it is inflicted), yet if the first man had not sinned, punishment would not be inflicted on his descendants without a previous fault: which St Thomas also affirms. But the Incarnation of the Son of God denotes not a penalty but rather a benefit.

paras.t: Duodecimo quæritur, an de costa Adæ poterat Eva formari. Et apparet quod non, quoniam ex tam parva materia nequivit fieri corpus tam grande, nisi forte per rarefactionem : corpus autem Evæ non erat rarum, sed grossum, spissum ac solidum. Respondetur, quod de hoc duæ sunt opiniones. Una Hugonis et Magistri Sententiarum, qui dicunt corpus Evæ formatum ex costa illa absque additione alicujus exterioris materiæ, per creationem aut conversionem alicujus in ipsam. Si enim (ut aiunt) Deus potuit materiam de nihilo facere, potuit eam in se ipsa multiplicare absque alicujus additione. Alii dicunt quod factum sit illud per additionem alterius materiæ, et probabilius reputat Thomas, quod factum sit hoc per additionem materiæ præexsistentis, eo quod Sancti communiter dicant, omnia ad minus in materia simul esse creata. Sed istis difficultatibus scholasticis, quæ super Sententias diffuse discutiuntur, nequaquam intendo immorari hoc loco.
paras.en: Twelfthly, it is asked whether Eve could be formed from Adam's rib. And it appears not, since so great a body could not be made from so small a matter, except perhaps by rarefaction: but the body of Eve was not rare, but gross, thick and solid. The answer is that there are two opinions about this. One is that of Hugh and of the Master of the Sentences, who say that the body of Eve was formed from that rib without the addition of any outside matter, whether by creation or by the conversion of something into it. For if (as they say) God could make matter out of nothing, he could multiply it in itself without the addition of anything. Others say that it was done by the addition of other matter; and Thomas judges it more probable that it was done by the addition of pre-existing matter, because the Saints commonly say that all things were created together, at least in their matter. But I by no means intend to linger in this place over these scholastic difficulties, which are discussed at length on the Sentences.

paras.t: Tertiodecimo quæritur, qualiter costa de qua facta est Eva, fuit primo in Adam. Aut enim fuit ei superflua, aut de ejus integritate consistens. Si secundum, ergo ea sublata, factus est imperfectus ac diminutus. Si primum, ergo fuit monstruosus, sicut qui habet sex digitos. Monstrum quippe est effectus suæ inconveniens speciei. Respondetur brevissime, quod costa illa fuit Adæ necessaria secundum quod erat suæ speciei principium, non in quantum fuit individuum certum. Ideo costa ablata, mansit integer homo.
paras.en: Thirteenthly, it is asked in what way the rib from which Eve was made was in Adam to begin with. For either it was superfluous to him, or it belonged to his integrity. If the second, then, when it was taken away, he was made imperfect and diminished. If the first, then he was monstrous, like one who has six fingers; for a monster is an effect unbefitting its species. The answer, very briefly, is that that rib was necessary to Adam inasmuch as he was the principle of his species, not inasmuch as he was a particular individual. Therefore, when the rib was taken away, the man remained whole.

paras.t: Quartodecimo quæritur, an Eva fuerit filia Adæ. Et apparet quod imo, quia ex substantia ejus est facta. Costa namque magis fuit de substantia Adæ, quam semen. Respondetur quod formatio Evæ non exstitit per naturalem generationem, sed per supernaturalem plasmationem, idcirco non exstitit filia Adæ.
paras.en: Fourteenthly, it is asked whether Eve was Adam's daughter. And it appears that she was, since she was made of his substance; for the rib was more of the substance of Adam than seed is. The answer is that the formation of Eve was not by natural generation but by a supernatural fashioning; therefore she was not Adam's daughter.

paras.t: Postremo circa illud, Ædificavit Dominus costam quam tulerat, etc., Lyra allegat et approbat Rabbi Salomonem, dicentem : Formatio mulieris describitur nomine ædificationis, quoniam sicut ædificium communiter grossius latiusque est inferius, quam supra, sic corpora mulierum communiter grossiora inferius, et subtiliora exstant superius. Et hoc propter debilitatem calidi naturalis in muliere, propter quod major pars alimenti manet inferius. Sed circa hoc scribit Rabbi Paulus, quod istud sit improprie dictum, inconveniensque ad propositum declarandum : quoniam ad Scripturam nil pertinet, an mulier sit grossior inferius, annon. Ideo aliam rationem adducit, dicendo quod sicut in ædificio manet eadem res numero in ædificato, quæ fuit ante ædificationem, et ex qua ædificium fit, ut patet dum ex lignis et saxis fit domus, ita dicit quod inter Adam et Evam mansit quodammodo individualis identitas, in quantum eadem costa numero mansit in Eva, quæ ante fuit in Adam. Sed istud satis imperite prolatum censetur. Dum enim ex aqua fit aer, non manet identitas individualis inter aquam et aerem, quamvis materia prima eadem numero perseveret in aere quæ fuit in aqua : sic quamvis costa in Eva mansit eadem numero, quantum ad primam materiam quæ fuit in Adam, non tamen ob hoc mansit eadem numero costa in utrisque, quoniam sub alia forma substantiali stetit in Adam quam in Eva. Quemadmodum autem materia sumit esse a forma substantiali, ita et distinctionem, unitatem aut numerationem a forma sortitur.
paras.en: Lastly, concerning the words [[2:22|the Lord God built the rib which he took|Ædificavit Dominus costam quam tulerat]], etc., Lyra cites and approves Rabbi Solomon, who says: The forming of the woman is described under the name of building because, as a building is commonly thicker and broader below than above, so women's bodies are commonly thicker below and slenderer above. And this is because of the weakness of the natural heat in woman, on account of which the greater part of the nourishment remains below. But on this Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos, the convert from Judaism whose Additions to Lyra Denis often cites] writes that this is said improperly and is unfitting to declare the point in hand, since it is no concern of Scripture whether woman is thicker below or not. He therefore brings another reason, saying that, as in a building the same thing in number [that is, the very same individual thing, not merely the same in kind] remains in what is built that was there before the building, and out of which the building is made, as is plain when a house is made of timber and stones, so, he says, between Adam and Eve there remained in some way an individual identity, inasmuch as the same rib in number remained in Eve that had been in Adam before. But this is judged to be said unskilfully enough. For when air is made from water, no individual identity remains between the water and the air, although the same prime matter [that is, the formless matter underlying every bodily substance] in number continues in the air that was in the water: so, although the rib remained in Eve the same in number as to the prime matter that was in Adam, yet not for that reason did the same rib in number remain in both, since it stood under one substantial form in Adam and under another in Eve. For as matter takes its being from the substantial form, so too it receives from the form its distinction, unity or number.

paras.t: Possent demum circa hunc passum alia dubia multa moveri, videlicet quamdiu fuit Adam in paradiso, et quamdiu formatio ejus introductionem ejus in paradisum præcessit, ac consimilia, quæ in expositione sequentis tangentur capituli.
paras.en: Many other doubts could finally be raised about this passage, namely how long Adam was in paradise, and how long his formation preceded his being brought into paradise, and the like; these will be touched on in the exposition of the following chapter.

2.title: Elucidatio spiritualis ejusdem capituli
2.title_en: Spiritual explanation of the same chapter

paras.t: Igitur perfecti sunt cœli et terra, et omnis ornatus eorum. Per cœlos angelici intellectus, per terram mentes humanæ recte intelliguntur, qui omnes perfecti sunt, quando angeli electi ad Deum conversi, per dona gloriæ sunt beatificati et roborati, imo et plene consummati in Deo, homines quoque per dona gratiæ gratum facientis formati. Denique ceteræ universæ creaturæ completionem quamdam sortiri videntur, dum electis hominibus, propter quos specialiter factæ sunt, obsequuntur. Rursus, per cœlos intelliguntur contemplativi et religiosi ac præsidentes; per terram, activi sæculares ac subditi, qui omnes in Ecclesia sunt suo modo perfecti, dum unusquisque eorum secundum exigentiam suæ vocationis digne Deo conversatur, quorum omnium ornatus, sunt virtutes ac dona Spiritus Sancti et meritorii actus.
paras.en: [[2:1|So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them|Igitur perfecti sunt cœli et terra, et omnis ornatus eorum]]. By the heavens the angelic intellects, and by the earth human minds, are rightly understood; and all of these were finished when the elect angels, turned to God, were beatified and strengthened by the gifts of glory, indeed fully consummated in God, and men too were formed by the gifts of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*: the grace that makes one pleasing to God]. Lastly, all the other creatures seem to obtain a certain completion while they serve elect men, for whose sake especially they were made. Again, by the heavens are understood contemplatives and religious and those who preside; by the earth, men of the active life, seculars and subjects: all of whom are finished in the Church, each in his own way, so long as each of them lives worthily before God according to the demands of his calling; and the furniture of all of these is the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost and meritorious acts.

paras.t: Complevitque Deus die septimo opus suum. Per septimum diem, intelligit Isidorus diem glorificationis et requietionis electorum in regno cælesti: in quo die requiescet Deus plenissime in electis glorificatis, faciendo eos plene et contentative conquiescere in se, ita ut satiati plenarie, nil plus neque quid amplius queant appetere. Denique illi diei, id est electis et beatis in die illo æternitatis, Deus plenissime benedicet per infusionem seu conservationem et consummationem munerum gloriæ.
paras.en: [[2:2|And on the seventh day God ended his work|Complevitque Deus die septimo opus suum]]. By the seventh day Isidore understands the day of the glorification and rest of the elect in the heavenly kingdom: on which day God will rest most fully in the glorified elect, by making them rest fully and contentedly in himself, so that, wholly satisfied, they can desire nothing more or anything further. Lastly, God will bless that day, that is, the elect and blessed in that day of eternity, most fully, by the infusion, or the preservation, and the consummation of the gifts of glory.

paras.t: Istæ sunt generationes cæli et terræ, in die quo fecit Dominus cælum et terram. Generationes naturales sunt, per quas res temporales acquirunt esse substantiale specificum. Generationes autem spirituales, sunt reformationes per quas creaturæ rationales acquirunt esse spirituale, quod est esse gratiæ ac virtutum. Istæ ergo sunt generationes cœli et terræ, id est, reformationes contemplativorum et activorum hominum in hoc mundo, quæ reformationes fiunt (sicut prætactum est) per infusionem charismatum Spiritus Sancti, præsertim per gratiam gratificantem: quando creatæ sunt, hoc est, spiritualiter regeneratæ ac reformatæ sunt; in die quo fecit Deus cœlum et terram, id est tempore evangelicæ lucis, quod est tempus gratiæ, in quo misericordia Dei plures convertit præter solitum, de quo die loquitur Isaias: In die illa erit germen Domini in gloria et magnificentia.
paras.en: [[2:4|These are the generations of the heaven and the earth|Istæ sunt generationes cæli et terræ]], [[2:4|in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth|in die quo fecit Dominus cælum et terram]]. Natural generations are those by which temporal things acquire their substantial and specific being. Spiritual generations are reformations, by which rational creatures acquire spiritual being, which is the being of grace and of the virtues. These, then, are [[2:4|the generations of the heaven and the earth|generationes cœli et terræ]], that is, the reformations of contemplative and active men in this world; which reformations come about (as was touched on above) through the infusion of the charisms of the Holy Ghost, above all through sanctifying grace: [[2:4|when they were created|quando creatæ sunt]], that is, were spiritually regenerated and reformed; [[2:4|in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth|in die quo fecit Deus cœlum et terram]], that is, in the time of the light of the Gospel, which is the time of grace, in which the mercy of God converts more than it was wont; of which day Isaias speaks: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory|In die illa erit germen Domini in gloria et magnificentia]].

paras.t: Et omne virgultum agri, id est incipientes fortiter proficientes, qui instar virgulti virent virore virtutum ac gratiæ, et ornantur ornatu quotidiani profectus; omnemque herbam regionis, id est universas animas christifideles, quæ sunt herbæ et fructus quidam regionis, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, in qua per fidem et caritatem regnat rex Christus; priusquam germinaret, id est, priusquam Ecclesia boni aliquid operaretur. Non enim aliquid meritorium operaretur, nisi prælato modo a Deo præveniatur ac fecundetur: ideo subditur, Necdum pluerat Dominus Deus super terram, id est habitatoribus terræ nondum infuderat aquam sapientiæ salutaris, atque cœlestis gratiæ imbrem. Et potest hoc loco per terram specialiter designari gentilitas, quæ ante suam conversionem erat quasi aridissima terra, quantum ad hoc quod carebat omni supernorum humore charismatum, ita quod dicere potuit Deo: Anima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi. Itaque nondum pluerat Dominus super terram, quando gentilitatem nondum instruxerat Scripturis novi ac veteris Testamenti. Et homo non erat qui operaretur terram. Tunc enim non erant prædicatores et prælati missi ad gentilitatem, qui corda gentilium vomere prædicationis ad pœnitentiam scinderent, virtutibusque excolerent, et disciplina exercerent morali, ita quod tunc in gentilibus implebatur quod Deus loquitur per Prophetam: Mandabo nubibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem. Præterea tunc non erat homo qui operaretur terram, quia infidelium nullus corpus suum tunc debite castigavit, nec cordis sui agrum fecundavit virtutibus. Omnes enim declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt. Hoc quoque convenit unicuique carnali et negligenti.
paras.en: [[2:5|And every plant of the field|Et omne virgultum agri]], that is, beginners making strong progress, who like a plant are green with the greenness of the virtues and of grace, and are adorned with the adornment of daily progress; [[2:5|and every herb of the ground|omnemque herbam regionis]], that is, all the faithful souls of Christ, which are the herbs and a kind of fruit of the region, that is, of the Church militant, in which Christ the King reigns through faith and charity [Denis reads *regionis*, "of the region", where the Douay-Rheims has "of the ground", and plays on it with *regnat*, "reigns"]; [[2:5|before it grew|priusquam germinaret]], that is, before the Church did anything good. For she would do nothing meritorious unless she were prevented and made fruitful by God in the manner stated above [prevented: that is, gone before by grace]: therefore it is added, [[2:5|for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth|Necdum pluerat Dominus Deus super terram]], that is, he had not yet poured into the dwellers on earth the water of saving wisdom and the shower of heavenly grace. And in this place the earth may specially designate the Gentiles, who before their conversion were like the driest earth, in that they lacked all moisture of heavenly charisms, so that they could say to God: [[Ps 142:6|my soul is as earth without water unto thee|Anima mea sicut terra sine aqua tibi]]. So [[2:5|the Lord God had not rained upon the earth|nondum pluerat Dominus super terram]] while he had not yet instructed the Gentiles with the Scriptures of the New and the Old Testament. And [[2:5|there was not a man to till the earth|Et homo non erat qui operaretur terram]]. For then there were no preachers and prelates sent to the Gentiles, to break up the hearts of the Gentiles for repentance with the ploughshare of preaching, to cultivate them with virtues and to exercise them in moral discipline; so that what God says by the Prophet was then fulfilled in the Gentiles: [[Is 5:6|I will command the clouds to rain no rain upon it|Mandabo nubibus meis, ne pluant super eam imbrem]]. Moreover, [[2:5|there was not a man to till the earth|non erat homo qui operaretur terram]] then, because none of the unbelievers then duly chastised his body, nor made the field of his heart fruitful with virtues. For [[Ps 13:3|They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together|Omnes enim declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt]]. This too fits every carnal and negligent man.

paras.t: Sed fons ascendebat e terra. Fons iste est Christus, de quo illud Ecclesiastici, Fons sapientiæ Verbum Dei in excelsis, rite accipitur, qui ascendit de terra, quando de Virgine natus est, de qua loquitur Isaias: Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem: quam terram nullus operatus est homo, quoniam nullus virorum Virginem fecundavit ut pareret Christum, qui est lapis de monte præcisus sine manibus, hoc est de regno ac populo Judæorum sine humano opere natus. Insuper fons iste, de quo ait Psalmista ad Patrem, Quoniam apud te est fons vitæ, fuit irrigans universam superficiem terræ, videlicet totam Ecclesiam, omnemque gentilitatem per Apostolorum et apostolicorum virorum doctrinam, quibus locutus est: Eritis mihi testes usque ad ultimum terræ. Nempe in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum. Unde per Isaiam Patri locutus est Filio: Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ.
paras.en: [[2:6|But a spring rose out of the earth|Sed fons ascendebat e terra]]. This spring is Christ, of whom that saying of Ecclesiasticus is rightly taken, [[Ecclus 1:5|The word of God on high is the fountain of wisdom|Fons sapientiæ Verbum Dei in excelsis]]; who rose out of the earth when he was born of the Virgin, of whom Isaias speaks: [[Is 45:8|let the earth be opened, and bud forth a saviour|Aperiatur terra, et germinet Salvatorem]]: an earth which no man tilled, since no man made the Virgin fruitful that she might bear Christ, who is the stone cut out of the mountain without hands[[Dan 2:45||]], that is, born of the kingdom and people of the Jews without human work. Moreover this spring, of which the Psalmist says to the Father, [[Ps 35:10|For with thee is the fountain of life|Quoniam apud te est fons vitæ]], was [[2:6|watering all the surface of the earth|irrigans universam superficiem terræ]], namely the whole Church and all the Gentiles, through the teaching of the Apostles and of apostolic men, to whom he said: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me|Eritis mihi testes]] [[Acts 1:8|even to the uttermost part of the earth|usque ad ultimum terræ]]. For indeed [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]. Hence by Isaias the Father said to the Son: [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]].

paras.t: Formavit igitur Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ, id est, Spiritus Sanctus corpus Christi formavit ex purissimis sanguinibus Virginis sacræ, et Christus ex sanctis patribus natus est, juxta illud Apostoli: Factus est ex semine David secundum carnem. Et inspiravit in faciem ejus spiraculum vitæ. Interior facies hominis, est mens ejus. Inspiravit ergo Deus Pater seu Trinitas tota in faciem Christi spiraculum vitæ, id est, Spiritum Sanctum menti ejus humanæ infudit copiosissime. Non enim ad mensuram dedit Deus Spiritum homini Christo, qui in Isaia testatur: Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me. De quo idem cecinit Isaias: Requiescet super eum Spiritus Domini. Et factus est homo in animam viventem: id est, Christus accepit in suæ incarnationis exordio animam viventem, non solum vita gratiæ in gradu altissimo gratiæ gratificantis, sed etiam vita gloriæ, quantum ad beatificam deitatis fruitionem plenissime, quantum ad superiorem suæ animæ portionem. Eodem enim instanti quo anima Christi creata est, impleta est plenitudine gratiarum et lumine gloriæ atque clarissima divinæ essentiæ visione per speciem, in quantum se extendebat capacitas mentis creatæ.
paras.en: [[2:7|the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth|Formavit igitur Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ]], that is, the Holy Ghost formed the body of Christ from the most pure blood of the sacred Virgin, and Christ was born of the holy fathers, according to that saying of the Apostle: He was made [[Rom 1:3|of the seed of David, according to the flesh|ex semine David secundum carnem]]. [[2:7|and breathed into his face the breath of life|Et inspiravit in faciem ejus spiraculum vitæ]]. The inner face of man is his mind. God the Father, then, or the whole Trinity, breathed into the face of Christ the breath of life, that is, poured the Holy Ghost most abundantly into his human mind. For [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|Non enim ad mensuram dedit Deus Spiritum]] to the man Christ, who testifies in Isaias: [[Is 61:1|The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me|Spiritus Domini super me, eo quod unxerit me]]. Of him the same Isaias sang: [[Is 11:2|the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him|Requiescet super eum Spiritus Domini]]. [[2:7|and man became a living soul|Et factus est homo in animam viventem]]: that is, at the very beginning of his incarnation Christ received a living soul, living not only with the life of grace, in the highest degree of sanctifying grace, but also with the life of glory, as to the most full beatific enjoyment of the Godhead, as regards the higher portion of his soul. For in the same instant in which the soul of Christ was created, it was filled with the fullness of graces and with the light of glory and with the most clear vision of the divine essence *per speciem* [that is, by open sight, as the blessed see God, not by faith], so far as the capacity of a created mind extended.

paras.t: Plantaverat autem Dominus Deus paradisum voluptatis a principio. Paradisus voluptatis, est Ecclesia militans, quæ in membris suis electis ac virtuosis, spiritualibus deliciis affluit, atque in isto exsilio dulcissime visitatur et consolatur a Deo. Hanc Deus ab exordio sæculi cœpit plantare, præsertim a tempore Abel justi, id est, per divina charismata stabilire ac radicare in mundo: de qua plantatione ait in Evangelio Dominus: Omnis plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur. In quo posuit hominem quem formaverat: id est, Christum constituit caput totius Ecclesiæ, sicut loquitur Paulus: Ipsum dedit caput super omnem Ecclesiam, quæ est corpus ipsius. Constituit quoque Christum hominem in ipsa Ecclesia, quia dum venit temporis plenitudo, misit Deus Filium suum, qui in terris est visus, et cum hominibus conversatus, quibus locutus est: Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat. Unde et Patri fatetur: In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te.
paras.en: Now [[2:8|the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure from the beginning|Plantaverat autem Dominus Deus paradisum voluptatis a principio]]. The paradise of pleasure is the Church militant, which in her elect and virtuous members abounds in spiritual delights, and in this exile is most sweetly visited and consoled by God. God began to plant her from the beginning of the world, especially from the time of Abel the just, that is, to establish her and root her in the world by divine charisms: of which planting the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Matt 15:13|Every plant which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up|Omnis plantatio quam non plantavit Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur]]. [[2:8|wherein he placed man whom he had formed|In quo posuit hominem quem formaverat]]: that is, he made Christ head of the whole Church, as Paul says: [[Eph 1:22|hath made him head over all the church|Ipsum dedit caput super omnem Ecclesiam]], [[Eph 1:23|Which is his body|quæ est corpus ipsius]]. He also set Christ as man in the Church itself, since [[Gal 4:4|when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son|dum venit temporis plenitudo, misit Deus Filium suum]], who was seen on earth and conversed with men, to whom he said: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|Ego in medio vestrum sum sicut qui ministrat]]. Hence he also confesses to the Father: [[Ps 21:23|in the midst of the church will I praise thee|In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te]].

paras.t: Produxit autem Dominus Deus de humo omne lignum pulchrum visu et ad vescendum suave: id est, omnem hominem virtuosum, qui ab exordio exstitit mundi, Deus de terra formavit, quantum ad esse naturæ; et quantum ad esse gratiæ ac virtutum, produxit tempore evangelicæ legis omnem Christifidelem de Ecclesia, in quantum ministerio Ecclesiæ omnis talis est per Baptismum spiritualiter regeneratus, quemadmodum ait Salvator: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest videre regnum Dei. Porro Christifidelis dicitur lignum, juxta illud: Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur. Nam et Christus de se ipso loquens: Si in viridi, inquit, ligno hæc faciunt, in arido quid fiet? Tale lignum est pulchrum visu, quia ornatum pulchritudine gratiæ et splendore sapientiæ ac virtutum. Est item ad vescendum suave, quoniam dulciter reficit alios verbo ac opere seu consolatione et gaudio spirituali, sicut de Tito loquitur Paulus Corinthiis: Refectus est spiritus ejus ab omnibus vobis. Et rursus ad Philemonem: Refice, ait, viscera mea in Domino. Produxit etiam Deus lignum vitæ in medio paradisi, videlicet Christum, de quo Salomon contestatur, quod Sapientia lignum vitæ est omnibus apprehendentibus eam, de quo Paulus: Nos, inquit, prædicamus Christum Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam. Lignumque scientiæ boni et mali. Per lignum hoc potest designari et Christus, de quo loquitur Isaias: Butyrum et mel comedet, ut sciat reprobare malum, et eligere bonum. Ipse enim plenissime docuit inter bonum et malum discernere. Potest item per lignum scientiæ boni et mali, liberum arbitrium accipi, propter causam mox exprimendam.
paras.en: [[2:9|the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold, and pleasant to eat of|Produxit autem Dominus Deus de humo omne lignum pulchrum visu et ad vescendum suave]]: that is, every virtuous man who has existed since the beginning of the world God formed from the earth as to the being of nature; and as to the being of grace and of the virtues, in the time of the law of the Gospel he brought forth every one of Christ's faithful from the Church, inasmuch as every such person is spiritually regenerated by Baptism through the ministry of the Church, as the Saviour says: [[John 3:5|unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God|Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest videre regnum Dei]] [Denis reads *videre*, "see", as at John 3:3, where the verse has "enter into"]. Further, one of Christ's faithful is called a tree [*lignum*, "wood" or "tree"], according to that saying: [[Matt 3:10|Every tree therefore that doth not yield good fruit, shall be cut down|Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur]]. For Christ too, speaking of himself: [[Luke 23:31|if in the green|Si in viridi]], he says, [[Luke 23:31|wood they do these things, what shall be done in the dry?|ligno hæc faciunt, in arido quid fiet?]]? Such a tree is fair to behold, because it is adorned with the beauty of grace and the splendour of wisdom and of the virtues. It is also pleasant to eat of, since it sweetly refreshes others by word and deed, or by consolation and spiritual joy, as Paul says of Titus to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 7:13|his spirit was refreshed by you all|Refectus est spiritus ejus ab omnibus vobis]]. And again to Philemon: [[Philem 1:20|Refresh|Refice]], he says, [[Philem 1:20|my bowels in the Lord|viscera mea in Domino]]. God also brought forth [[2:9|the tree of life also in the midst of paradise|lignum vitæ in medio paradisi]], namely Christ, of whom Solomon testifies that Wisdom [[Prov 3:18|is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her|lignum vitæ est omnibus apprehendentibus eam]]; of whom Paul: We, he says, preach [[1 Cor 1:24|Christ, the power of God and the wisdom of God|Christum Dei virtutem et Dei sapientiam]]. [[2:9|and the tree of knowledge of good and evil|Lignumque scientiæ boni et mali]]. By this tree Christ too may be designated, of whom Isaias speaks: [[Is 7:15|He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know to refuse the evil, and to choose the good|Butyrum et mel comedet, ut sciat reprobare malum, et eligere bonum]]. For he most fully taught how to discern between good and evil. Again, by the tree of knowledge of good and evil free will may be understood, for a reason to be stated shortly.

paras.t: Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis: id est, Christus unigenitus Dei ex fonte paternæ mentis æterna generatione egressus est, et venit in mundum, naturam assumens humanam, quemadmodum fassus est: Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum; ad irrigandum paradisum, id est, Ecclesiam, sicut expositum est. Unde et ipse: Qui biberit, inquit, ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum; sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam. Qui deinde dividitur in quatuor capita: id est, per quatuor mundi partes rivos sapientiæ suæ diffudit, rorem gratiæ sparsit, et quatuor fluvios, utpote quatuor Evangelia, fluere atque decurrere fecit. Vel primus fluvius est totale Evangelium, a quatuor Evangelistis conscriptum; fluvius secundus, moralis doctrina epistolarum Pauli et aliorum quatuor Apostolorum; fluvius tertius, liber historialis Actuum Apostolorum: fluvius quartus, liber propheticus Apocalypsis. Denique fluvius iste in quatuor dividitur capita, dum ait Apostolus: Christus factus est nobis a Deo sapientia et justitia et sanctificatio et redemptio.
paras.en: [[2:10|And a river went out of the place of pleasure|Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis]]: that is, Christ, the only-begotten of God, went forth from the fountain of the Father's mind by eternal generation, and came into the world, taking human nature, as he confessed: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father and am come into the world|Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum]]; [[2:10|to water paradise|ad irrigandum paradisum]], that is, the Church, as has been explained. Hence he himself says: [[John 4:13|he that shall drink|Qui biberit]], he says, [[John 4:13|of the water that I will give him shall not thirst for ever|ex aqua quam ego dabo ei, non sitiet in æternum]]; [[John 4:14|But the water that I will give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|sed aqua quam ego dabo ei, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]. [[2:10|which from thence is divided into four heads|Qui deinde dividitur in quatuor capita]]: that is, he poured out the streams of his wisdom through the four parts of the world, sprinkled the dew of grace, and made four rivers, namely the four Gospels, to flow and run. Or the first river is the whole Gospel, written by the four Evangelists; the second river, the moral teaching of the epistles of Paul and of four other Apostles; the third river, the historical book of the Acts of the Apostles; the fourth river, the prophetic book of the Apocalypse. Lastly, this river is divided into four heads when the Apostle says: Christ [[1 Cor 1:30|of God is made unto us wisdom and justice and sanctification and redemption|factus est nobis a Deo sapientia et justitia et sanctificatio et redemptio]].

paras.t: Nomen uni Phison. Per Phison, qui interpretatur (secundum Glossam) mutatio oris, intelligi potest Evangelium sancti Joannis, in quo diffusius edocetur, qualiter Verbum caro factum sit, ita quod quasi mutatus apparet formam servi accipiens, quamvis non in Verbi deitate, sed in assumpta humanitate sit facta mutatio. Ipse est qui circuit omnem terram Hevilath. Per terram Hevilath seu Indiam, significantur ferventes et contemplativi, in quibus sapientia Evangelii sancti Joannis specialiter fluit ac viget. In quibus nascitur aurum, videlicet fervor pretiosissimus divini amoris, qui est optimum aurum. Ibique invenitur bdellium. Per bdellium quæ est aromatica arbor, cujus gutta est lucida et gustu amara ac boni odoris, intelligitur dolor contritionis, et deploratio præsentis exsilii, quæ in contemplativis constat, quoniam quotidiana sua peccata acri contritione deplangunt, ad patriamque adspirant cœlestem, dicentes: Heu mihi quia incolatus meus prolongatus est. Et, Fuerunt mihi lacrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte. Et lapis onychinus, per quem designatur conversatio humana exterior exemplaris, caritasque fraterna, quoniam onyx similitudinem habet coloris unguis humani; contemplativi autem in vita hac quandocumque ad divina rapiuntur, tamen sæpe coguntur ad humanam vitam redire et aliis conformari.
paras.en: [[2:11|The name of the one is Phison|Nomen uni Phison]]. By Phison, which is interpreted (according to the Gloss) *change of mouth*, may be understood the Gospel of St John, in which it is taught more fully how the Word was made flesh, so that he appears as it were changed, [[Phil 2:7|taking the form of a servant|formam servi accipiens]], although the change was made not in the Godhead of the Word but in the humanity assumed. [[2:11|that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath|Ipse est qui circuit omnem terram Hevilath]]. By the land of Hevilath, or India, are signified the fervent and the contemplatives, in whom the wisdom of the Gospel of St John especially flows and thrives. In them [[2:11|gold groweth|nascitur aurum]], namely the most precious fervour of divine love, which is the best gold. [[2:12|there is found bdellium|Ibique invenitur bdellium]]. By bdellium, which is an aromatic tree whose gum is clear, bitter to the taste and of good odour, is understood the sorrow of contrition and the lamenting of this present exile, which is found in contemplatives, since they bewail their daily sins with sharp contrition and long for the heavenly fatherland, saying: [[Ps 119:5|Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged!|Heu mihi quia incolatus meus prolongatus est]] And: [[Ps 41:4|My tears have been my bread day and night|Fuerunt mihi lacrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte]]. [[2:12|and the onyx stone|Et lapis onychinus]], by which is designated an exemplary outward human conduct and brotherly charity, since the onyx has the likeness of the colour of a man's nail [*onyx* is Greek for "nail"]; for contemplatives in this life, however they are at times rapt to divine things, are yet often compelled to return to human life and conform themselves to others.

paras.t: Et nomen fluvii secundi, Gehon. Per Gehon, qui interpretatur hiatus terræ, intelligitur Evangelium sancti Matthæi, in quo specialiter edocemur terræ hiatum, id est cupiditatem omnem vitare, seu bonum hiatum, utpote ferventem affectum futurorum bonorum habere. Qui circuit omnem terram Æthiopiæ. Ibi quippe ad litteram Evangelium hoc abundantius fluxit ac fusum est. Tota quoque gentilitas, quæ erat vitiorum nigredine cooperta, per Æthiopiam explicatur, et Evangelium istud hausit atque potavit.
paras.en: [[2:13|And the name of the second river is Gehon|Et nomen fluvii secundi, Gehon]]. By Gehon, which is interpreted *gaping of the earth*, is understood the Gospel of St Matthew, in which we are especially taught to shun the gaping of the earth, that is, all cupidity, or to have a good gaping, namely a fervent longing for the good things to come. [[2:13|that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia|Qui circuit omnem terram Æthiopiæ]]. For there, to the letter, this Gospel flowed and was poured out more abundantly. Also the whole of the Gentiles, who were covered with the blackness of vices, are signified by Ethiopia; and they drew this Gospel and drank it.

paras.t: Nomen vero fluminis tertii, Tigris. Per Tigrim Evangelium sancti Lucæ exprimitur, quod instar tigridis velocissimæ undique est vulgatum atque receptum, quia non solum Catholicis, sed et hæreticis ac Sarracenis specialiter placuit; propter quod super Lucam asserit Origenes: Innumerabiles hæretici sunt, qui Evangelium secundum Lucam recipiunt. Denique in Alcorano Mahometi perfidi et mendosi, plura ex Evangelio Lucæ sumpta habentur. Hoc Evangelium pertransit Assyrios. Assyrii interpretantur dirigentes. Veraciter autem fideles secundum Christi doctrinam se dirigunt, et ita Evangelium Lucæ plene et recte acceptant. Fluvius autem quartus, ipse est Euphrates, quod interpretatur frugifer, et Evangelium sancti Marci significat, quo ad virtutum fructificationem instruimur.
paras.en: [[2:14|the name of the third river is Tigris|Nomen vero fluminis tertii, Tigris]]. By the Tigris is expressed the Gospel of St Luke, which like a most swift tigress [*tigris* is both the river and the tiger] has been everywhere published and received, since it has pleased in a special way not only Catholics but also heretics and Saracens; for which reason Origen asserts, on Luke: There are countless heretics who receive the Gospel according to Luke. Indeed, in the Alcoran of the faithless and lying Mahomet many things taken from the Gospel of Luke are found. This Gospel [[2:14|passeth along by the Assyrians|pertransit Assyrios]]. *Assyrians* is interpreted *directing*. And truly the faithful direct themselves according to the doctrine of Christ, and so accept the Gospel of Luke fully and rightly. [[2:14|And the fourth river is Euphrates|Fluvius autem quartus, ipse est Euphrates]], which is interpreted *fruitful*, and signifies the Gospel of St Mark, by which we are instructed in bearing the fruit of the virtues.

paras.t: Tulit ergo Dominus Deus hominem, id est, Christum secundum naturam assumptam eduxit de inviolatissimo Virginis utero, sicut in Psalmo fatetur: Quoniam tu es qui extraxisti me de ventre. Et posuit eum in paradisum voluptatis, id est, totius Ecclesiæ principem, legislatorem et illuminatorem ipsum effecit, juxta quod ait per Isaiam: Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus. Ut operaretur et custodiret illum, id est, corda fidelium per dona gratiæ suæ fecundaret et exerceret, atque in bonis conservaret fideles, sicut in Evangelio ait: Pater, quos dedisti mihi, non perdidi quemquam ex eis. Itemque: Quum essem cum eis, ego servabam eos: et quos dedisti mihi, custodivi.
paras.en: [[2:15|the Lord God took man|Tulit ergo Dominus Deus hominem]], that is, he brought Christ forth, according to the nature he assumed, from the most inviolate womb of the Virgin, as he confesses in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:10|For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb|Quoniam tu es qui extraxisti me de ventre]]. [[2:15|and put him into the paradise of pleasure|Et posuit eum in paradisum voluptatis]], that is, he made him the prince, lawgiver and enlightener of the whole Church, according to what he says by Isaias: [[Is 55:4|Behold I have given him for a witness to the people, for a leader and a master to the Gentiles|Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem ac præceptorem gentibus]]. [[2:15|to dress it, and to keep it|Ut operaretur et custodiret illum]], that is, to make fruitful and exercise the hearts of the faithful by the gifts of his grace, and to keep the faithful in good things, as he says in the Gospel: Father, [[John 18:9|Of them whom thou hast given me, I have not lost any one|quos dedisti mihi, non perdidi quemquam ex eis]]. And again: [[John 17:12|While I was with them, I kept them|Quum essem cum eis, ego servabam eos]]: [[John 17:12|Those whom thou gavest me have I kept|et quos dedisti mihi, custodivi]].

paras.t: Præcepitque ei, dicens: Ex omni ligno paradisi comede, id est, ex omni natione et plebe aliquos tibi per fidem et caritatem incorpora. Porro, quod Deus præceperit istud Christo homini, constat ex eo quod ipsemet profitetur: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. De ligno autem scientiæ boni et mali ne comedas, id est, vanos et sciolos, in oculis propriis sapientes, ac reprobos relinquas, nec membris tuis invisceres. Hinc Christus ad Patrem disseruit: Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi de mundo.
paras.en: [[2:16|he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat|Præcepitque ei, dicens: Ex omni ligno paradisi comede]], that is, out of every nation and people incorporate some into thyself through faith and charity. Further, that God gave this command to Christ as man is clear from what he himself professes: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. [[2:17|But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat|De ligno autem scientiæ boni et mali ne comedas]], that is, leave aside the vain and the smatterers, wise in their own eyes, and the reprobate, and do not take them into thy members. Hence Christ declared to the Father: [[John 17:9|I pray not for the world, but for them whom thou hast given me|Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi]] out of the world [Denis adds *de mundo*, "out of the world", from John 17:6].

paras.t: Dixit quoque Dominus Deus: Non est bonum, hominem esse solum, id est, non decet, nec expedit ut Christus in mundo infructuosus remaneat. Faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi, hoc est, Ecclesiam primitivam formemus ex eo, per cujus ministerium totus mundus regeneretur, et salvetur per ipsum.
paras.en: And [[2:18|the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone|Dixit quoque Dominus Deus: Non est bonum, hominem esse solum]], that is, it is not fitting nor expedient that Christ should remain fruitless in the world. [[2:18|let us make him a help like unto himself|Faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi]], that is, let us form from him the primitive Church, by whose ministry the whole world may be regenerated, and be saved through him.

paras.t: Formatis igitur de humo cunctis animantibus, etc. Per hoc spiritualiter præfiguratum est, quod omnia genera hominum, qui secundum diversitatem vitiorum aut virtutum, diversis exprimuntur nominibus avium ac brutorum, Deus spiritualiter præsentavit animæ Christi, ad cognoscendum, et item ad intelligendum, qui ex eis essent electi, quibus juxta hoc Christus imposuit nomen. Adhuc vero non inveniebatur adjutor similis ejus, hoc est, Christo nullus electorum æqualis inventus est. Nec Christus invenit Sponsam illam in terra, propter quam ex se formandam descendit in mundum.
paras.en: So, [[2:19|the Lord God having formed out of the ground all the beasts|Formatis igitur de humo cunctis animantibus]], etc. By this it was spiritually prefigured that God spiritually presented to the soul of Christ all the kinds of men, who according to the diversity of their vices or virtues are expressed by the various names of birds and beasts, for him to know them, and also to understand which of them were elect; and on these, accordingly, Christ imposed a name. But as yet [[2:20|there was not found a helper like himself|non inveniebatur adjutor similis ejus]], that is, none of the elect was found equal to Christ. Nor did Christ find on earth that Bride for whose forming out of himself he came down into the world.

paras.t: Immisit ergo Dominus Deus soporem in Adam, id est, voluntatem subeundi mortem pro mundi salute Christo inspiravit, et eum in cruce mori voluit. Quumque obdormisset, tulit unam de costis ejus, hoc est, Christo in cruce defuncto, lancea militari latus ejus perforari permisit, imo et perforavit, eo modo quo beatissimus princeps Apostolorum testatur: Deus qui præenuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic. Sicque formavit ex eo Ecclesiam, quoniam sacramenta quibus formatur Ecclesia, de latere Christi perfosso fluxerunt. Omnia etenim sacramenta, omnem suam virtutem a dominica passione et merito ejus sortita sunt. Et replevit carnem pro ea, id est, pro latere Christi, sic perforato, conjunxit et dedit ei Ecclesiam, quæ pretio sanguinis Christi redempta est et Christo unita, quemadmodum in Isaia legitur: Si posuerit animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum, et dispertiam ei plurimos.
paras.en: Then [[2:21|the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam|Immisit ergo Dominus Deus soporem in Adam]], that is, he inspired Christ with the will to undergo death for the salvation of the world, and willed that he should die on the cross. [[2:21|and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs|Quumque obdormisset, tulit unam de costis ejus]], that is, when Christ had died on the cross, he permitted his side to be pierced with a soldier's lance[[John 19:34||]], nay, he himself pierced it, in the way that the most blessed prince of the Apostles testifies: [[Acts 3:18|God before had shewed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled|Deus qui præenuntiavit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic]]. And so he formed the Church out of him, since the sacraments by which the Church is formed flowed from the pierced side of Christ. For all the sacraments have received all their power from the Lord's passion and its merit. [[2:21|and filled up flesh for it|Et replevit carnem pro ea]], that is, in place of the side of Christ thus pierced he joined and gave to him the Church, which was redeemed at the price of Christ's blood and united to Christ, as is read in Isaias: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed|Si posuerit animam suam pro peccato, videbit semen longævum]]; and: [[Is 53:12|Therefore will I distribute to him very many|dispertiam ei plurimos]] [the margin gives only Is. liii, 10; these last words are from v. 12].

paras.t: Et adduxit eam ad Adam, id est, Ecclesiam adduxit ad Christum, tanquam ad caput, per fidem, propter quod ait: Omne quod dat mihi Pater, ad me veniet.
paras.en: [[2:22|and brought her to Adam|Et adduxit eam ad Adam]], that is, he brought the Church to Christ, as to her head, through faith; for which reason he says: [[John 6:37|All that the Father giveth to me shall come to me|Omne quod dat mihi Pater, ad me veniet]].

paras.t: Dixitque Adam: Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea, id est, Ecclesia ista sanguine corporis mei formata est, et mihi tam cara est, ut proprium os et caro. Unde et Paulus testatur: Vos estis corpus Christi, et membra de membro. Hæc vocabitur virago, quoniam de viro sumpta est. Recte nomen istud Ecclesiæ competit, quæ de Christo est procreata, de qua cecinit Jeremias: Mulier circumdabit virum. Ecclesia quoque fortissima est in Deo, et virilissime agit, sicque virago rite vocatur.
paras.en: And [[2:23|Adam said: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh|Dixitque Adam: Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea]], that is, this Church has been formed by the blood of my body, and is as dear to me as my own bone and flesh [*cara*, "dear", echoes *caro*, "flesh"]. Hence Paul too testifies: [[1 Cor 12:27|you are the body of Christ and members of member|Vos estis corpus Christi, et membra de membro]]. [[2:23|she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man|Hæc vocabitur virago, quoniam de viro sumpta est]] [the Latin has *virago*, from *vir*, "man": a woman of manly strength]. This name rightly befits the Church, which was begotten of Christ, and of which Jeremias sang: [[Jer 31:22|A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Mulier circumdabit virum]]. The Church too is most strong in God, and acts most manfully, and so is rightly called *virago*.

paras.t: Quamobrem relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem: id est, Christus ipse Patrem suum quasi reliquit, veniendo in mundum, et matrem, utpote Synagogam, et adhæsit uxori suæ, id est Ecclesiæ. Factique sunt duo, scilicet Christus et Ecclesia, in carne una, id est, unum mysticum corpus constituunt, cujus principale caput est Christus.
paras.en: [[2:24|Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother|Quamobrem relinquet homo patrem suum et matrem]]: that is, Christ himself as it were left his Father by coming into the world, and his mother, namely the Synagogue, and cleaved to his wife, that is, the Church. And they were made [[2:24|two|duo]], namely Christ and the Church, [[2:24|in one flesh|in carne una]], that is, they make up one mystical body, whose principal head is Christ.

paras.t: Erat autem uterque nudus, Adam scilicet et uxor ejus, et non erubescebant. Sic Christus in mundo isto conversans, nudus et pauper fuit, nec inde erubuit: primitivaque Ecclesia exstitit nuda et egena, nec inde verecundabatur, sed gloriabatur in Domino.
paras.en: And [[2:25|they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed|Erat autem uterque nudus, Adam scilicet et uxor ejus, et non erubescebant]]. So Christ, living in this world, was naked and poor, and was not ashamed of it; and the primitive Church was naked and needy, and was not abashed thereby, but gloried in the Lord.

30.title: Closing lines (article title not in sample)
30.note: The sample begins mid-sentence at the end of this article.

paras.t: […]denter se habuit, ultra modum, id est valde et ultra solitum communemque ministrorum eventum, non tamen immoderate per culpæ excessum, quia juste sic accidit. Et habuit greges multos, ancillas et servos, camelos et asinos. Quocirca quæri potest, an Jacob usus sit prædicta industria circa oves et capras dumtaxat, an etiam circa ceterorum pecorum greges. Ad quod non videtur ex littera haberi certa et manifesta responsio; sed quoniam infra legitur Jacob eduxisse de Mesopotamia tantam multitudinem non solum ovium et caprarum, sed et vaccarum, asinorum et camelorum, videri potest alicui, quod etiam de illis sic fecerit.
paras.en: […] he fared abundantly, [[30:43|exceedingly|ultra modum]]: that is, greatly and beyond what is usual and the common lot of servants; yet not immoderately, through any excess of fault, for it came about justly. [[30:43|And he had many flocks, maid-servants and men-servants, camels and asses.|Et habuit greges multos, ancillas et servos, camelos et asinos.]] Here it may be asked whether Jacob used the device described above only with the sheep and goats, or with the flocks of the other animals as well. To this no certain and plain answer seems to be had from the letter; but since we read below that Jacob led out of Mesopotamia so great a multitude not only of sheep and goats but also of cows, asses and camels, it may seem to some that he did the same with these too.

30.title_en: Closing lines (article title not in sample)

30.title: De spirituali ejusdem capituli tricesimi intellectu

paras.t: Cernens autem Rachel quod infecunda esset, invidit sorori suæ, et ait marito suo: Da mihi liberos, alioqui moriar. Per Rachelem intelligitur anima contemplativa, quæ contemplationis suæ fructu interno et propriæ salutis profectibus non contenta, invidet suæ sorori fecundæ: id est, per modum invidentis se habet circa animam viri activi, in aliorum conversione et prædicationibus fructuosi, conquerens Sponso cœlesti, et rogans eumdem ut sibi det liberos, id est, per se alios convertat, reformet ac salvet. Cui Christus respondet, ex parte sui non esse defectum. Cui rursus hæc Rachel seu contemplatrix anima dicit, Habeo famulam, etc., id est, carnem istam mortalem cui conjuncta sum, illam fecunda, dando mihi gratiam ac virtutem, ut corpus meum ita afficiam flagellis, vigiliis, abstinentiis, fletibus, atque orationum instantiis, quatenus meritis horum corporalium exercitiorum meorum obtineam aliorum conversionem, eos quoque qui interdum me visitant, tam efficaciter horter et alloquar, ut convertantur atque salventur.
paras.en: [[30:1|And Rachel seeing herself without children, envied her sister, and said to her husband: Give me children, otherwise I shall die.|Cernens autem Rachel quod infecunda esset, invidit sorori suæ, et ait marito suo: Da mihi liberos, alioquin moriar.]] By Rachel is understood the contemplative soul, which, not content with the inward fruit of its contemplation and with progress in its own salvation, envies its fruitful sister: that is, it bears itself enviously toward the soul of the active man, who is fruitful in the conversion of others and in preaching, and it complains to the heavenly Bridegroom and begs Him to give it children, that is, to convert, reform and save others through it. Christ answers that the want is not on His part. Then this Rachel, the contemplative soul, says to Him again, [[30:3|I have here my servant|Habeo, inquit, famulam]], etc.; that is: This mortal flesh to which I am joined, make it fruitful, giving me grace and strength so to afflict my body with scourgings, vigils, fasts, tears and persevering prayer, that by the merits of these bodily exercises I may obtain the conversion of others, and may exhort and address those who sometimes visit me so effectively that they are converted and saved.

paras.t: Deditque illi Balam in conjugium. Bala interpretatur inveterata. Tunc ergo Bala traditur in conjugium Jacob, dum caro ex antiquo fomite vitiisque infecta, rationi subjicitur, et Sponso cœlesti ad serviendum offertur, juxta illud Apostoli, Exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam sanctam, viventem, Deo placentem (Rom. xii, 1): sicque Christus per carnis hujus obsequium spirituales generat filios.
paras.en: [[30:4|And she gave him Bala in marriage|Deditque illi Balam in conjugium]]. Bala is interpreted 'grown old.' Bala, then, is given in marriage to Jacob when the flesh, infected by the ancient tinder of sin and by vices, is made subject to reason and offered to the heavenly Bridegroom for His service, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 12:1|present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God|exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam viventem, sanctam, Deo placentem]]. And thus Christ, through the service of this flesh, begets spiritual children.

paras.t: Sentiens Lia quod parere desiisset, Zelpham ancillam suam marito tradidit: hoc est, anima viri activi, qui præ debilitate opera non valet misericordiæ amplius exercere, aliam quamcumque personam ei subservientem, Christo loco sui assignat, ut per illam fiant hujusmodi, et opera producantur virtutum.
paras.en: [[30:9|Lia perceiving that she had left of bearing, gave Zelpha, her handmaid, to her husband.|Sentiens Lia quod parere desiisset, Zelpham ancillam suam marito tradidit.]] That is: the soul of the active man who, through weakness, is no longer able to perform works of mercy, assigns to Christ in its own place some other person who serves it, so that through that person such things may be done and works of virtue brought forth.

paras.t: Amplius, per hoc quod Rachel desideravit mandragoras Liæ, ei a filio suo Ruben allatas, signatur quod anima contemplativa quandoque appetit bonæ famæ odorem, quam anima habet activa per opera fidei coram aliis facta, quæ designantur per Ruben primogenitum Liæ, qui filius visionis interpretatur, per quem opera fidei (quæ est spiritualis oculus animæ) intelliguntur. Lia autem respondet Racheli: Parumne tibi videtur quod præripueris maritum meum mihi, etc.: quoniam anima viri activi forinsecus occupata, frequenter conqueritur se a cœlestis Sponsi amplexibus impediri, et se potius quam proximi sui animam ad exteriora officia applicari. Cui tamen interdum anima contemplativa condescendens, favet ut ad tempus contemplationis vacet quieti, in Sponsi amplexibus quiescendo: sicque anima activi supernaturaliter fecundata et roborata, rursus generare et pristina virtutum exercitia exsequi incipit. Tandem recordatus Dominus Rachelis, aperit vulvam ejus, ita quod parit Joseph: hoc est, mentem contemplativam tanto implet zelo fraternæ salutis, quod merito affectionis tam sanctæ obtinet alicujus conversionem, per quod arbitratur se ab infecunditatis suæ ereptam opprobrio, nec tamen contentatur omnino, sed alterius quoque adhuc sitit salutem, dicens: Addat mihi Dominus filium alterum.
paras.en: Further, by Rachel's desiring Lia's [[30:14|mandrakes|mandragoras]], brought to her by her son Ruben, it is signified that the contemplative soul sometimes longs for the fragrance of a good name, which the active soul has through works of faith done in the sight of others. These are designated by Ruben, Lia's firstborn, whose name is interpreted 'son of vision,' by whom the works of faith are understood (faith being the spiritual eye of the soul). But Lia answers Rachel: [[30:15|Dost thou think it a small matter, that thou hast taken my husband from me|Parumne tibi videtur quod præripueris maritum mihi]], etc.: because the soul of the active man, busied with outward things, often complains that it is kept from the embraces of the heavenly Bridegroom, and that it, rather than its neighbour's soul, is set to outward duties. Yet the contemplative soul, sometimes condescending to it, allows it for a time to rest in the quiet of contemplation, reposing in the Bridegroom's embraces; and so the soul of the active man, supernaturally made fruitful and strengthened, begins again to bring forth and to take up its former exercises of virtue. At length [[30:22|the Lord also remembering Rachel|Recordatus quoque Dominus Rachelis]] opens her womb, so that she bears Joseph: that is, He fills the contemplative mind with such zeal for the salvation of its brethren that, by the merit of so holy an affection, it obtains someone's conversion, and by this judges itself delivered from the reproach of its barrenness. Yet it is not wholly content, but still thirsts for the salvation of another, saying: [[30:24|The Lord give me also another son.|Addat mihi Dominus filium alterum.]]

paras.t: Præterea, nato Joseph, voluit Jacob ad patriam suam reverti: quia dum Christus multos ex Synagoga tam activos quam contemplativos suo discipulatui conjunxisset, ac regnasset, voluit reverti ad Patrem, patriamque cœlestem. Vir quoque fidelis, contemplativæ vitæ fructu gustato, cupit exterioribus resignare, et interioribus pure insistere; quem Laban cupit adhuc in exterioribus et pristino suo detinere obsequio. Vir autem contemplativus, pensans quantum ex hoc Jacob possit fructificare, eo pacto consentit, ut oves et capræ diversorum colorum, sint suæ, id est, quatenus eos possit convertere, et spirituales suos efficere filios, qui duplicitatis vitio et maculis pravitatum sunt respersi. Cui Dominus in hoc aliquando acquiescit, ita quod orationibus, exhortationibus, meritis et exemplis viri talis, peccatores tales convertit; alios vero greges, scilicet justos, aliis committit pastoribus.
paras.en: Moreover, [[30:25|when Joseph was born|Nato autem Joseph]], Jacob wished to return to his own country: for when Christ had joined many from the Synagogue, both active and contemplative, to His discipleship, and had reigned, He wished to return to the Father and the heavenly fatherland. So too the faithful man, having tasted the fruit of the contemplative life, desires to give up outward things and to apply himself purely to inward ones; but Laban wishes to keep him still in outward things and in his former service. The contemplative man, however, weighing how much fruit Jacob might bear from this, consents on the condition that the sheep and goats of divers colours shall be his: that is, that he may convert those who are spattered with the vice of duplicity and the stains of wickedness, and make them his spiritual children. And the Lord sometimes grants him this, so that by the prayers, exhortations, merits and examples of such a man He converts such sinners; but the other flocks, namely the just, He entrusts to other shepherds.

paras.t: Itaque Jacob ovibus sibi creditis virgas decorticatas et multiformiter coloratas, tempore spiritualis fecundationis proponit, hoc est præcepta justitiæ, auctoritatem ecclesiasticam, potestatem verbi cœlestis, per quæ quasi per virgas corriguntur iniqui et reformantur ac diriguntur, quæ etiam virgæ multiplici sunt decore rectitudinis ac gratiæ decoratæ. Unde et lex Christi virga vocatur, juxta illud Psalmi: Virgam virtutis tuæ emittet Dominus ex Sion (Ps. cix, 2). Itemque: Virga æquitatis, seu virga directionis, virga regni tui (Ps. xliv, 7). Præterea in canalibus aquarum ponuntur hæ virgæ, id est, in libris sacræ Scripturæ (qui aquis sapientiæ salutaris et gratiarum fluentis repleti sunt) continentur descriptæ. Cortex vero a virgis detrahitur, dum superficialis et indiscretus intellectus, aut etiam rigor distortus, a præceptis et documentis atque ecclesiasticis auctoritatibus removetur, ne quis voluntate pro lege utatur, aut præcepta absque dispensatione et vera interpretatione juxta mentem legislatoris jubeat observari. Itaque per hæc oves et capræ, id est, fideles qui ante fuerunt diversitate vitiorum perfusi, fiunt varietate virtutum ornati, per quod homo qui præsidet eis, seu ita eosdem convertit, ultra modum ditatur sobole spirituali ac meritis in præsenti, præmiisque in futuro: quoniam omnium illorum opera bona et salus in ipsum redundant, et ipse cum singulis atque pro singulis coronatur; habetque asinos et camelos, utpote eos qui onus præceptorum cœlestium prompte ac obedientialiter portant. Alterutrum quoque onera sua pie supportant, quatenus omnes simul a Deo portari et misericordiam consequi mereantur, quemadmodum monet Apostolus: Alter alterius onera portate, et sic adimplebitis legem Christi (Gal. vi, 2).
paras.en: And so Jacob sets before the sheep entrusted to him, in the time of spiritual conceiving, rods stripped of bark and coloured in many ways: that is, the precepts of justice, the authority of the Church, the power of the heavenly word, by which, as by rods, the wicked are corrected, reformed and set straight; and these rods are adorned with the manifold beauty of uprightness and grace. Hence the law of Christ is also called a rod (virga), according to the Psalm: [[Ps 109:2|The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion|Virgam virtutis tuæ emittet Dominus ex Sion]]. And again: a rod of equity, or [[Ps 44:7|the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness|virga directionis virga regni tui]]. Further, these rods are placed in the troughs of water: that is, they are found written in the books of Holy Scripture, which are filled with the waters of saving wisdom and the streams of graces. The bark is stripped from the rods when a superficial and undiscerning understanding, or even a distorted rigour, is removed from the precepts, teachings and authorities of the Church, so that no one may use his own will in place of the law, or command precepts to be kept without dispensation and true interpretation according to the mind of the lawgiver. Thus by these means the sheep and goats, that is, the faithful who were before steeped in a diversity of vices, become adorned with a variety of virtues; and so [[30:43|the man was enriched exceedingly|Ditatusque est homo ultra modum]]: he who presides over them, or who so converts them, is enriched with spiritual offspring and merits in the present, and with rewards in the future; for the good works and salvation of all of them redound to him, and he is crowned with each and for each. And he has asses and camels, namely those who bear the burden of the heavenly precepts promptly and obediently. They also lovingly bear one another's burdens, so that all together may deserve to be carried by God and to obtain mercy, as the Apostle admonishes: [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens: and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ.|Alter alterius onera portate, et sic adimplebitis legem Christi.]]

30.title_en: On the spiritual sense of the same thirtieth chapter

31.title: Elucidatio capituli tricesimi primi: Postquam autem audivit verba filiorum Laban
31.note: The sample ends mid-sentence near the end of this article (v. 54).
